answer: The silver-smith bench holds coils of wire, the draw plate bolted to the edge. Proof of silver-smith via filigree ring tally — a ring the smith solders only after 35 rings hold their filigree without one loosening at the band, each soldered by the smith herself. knoll draws the wire through the plate till it runs even. sonnet coils the filigree tight and solders each join with flame. jetty polishes the ring on the buff and checks the band for a loose thread. Thirty-five rings must hold their filigree without one loosening at the band, and the next still loosens where the solder ran cold.
